discussions.name: NWS Seattle
synopsis: Precipitation chances will linger today as a weak system brings light rain to the lowlands and light snow to the Cascades. A weak ridge building over the Pacific Northwest will bring a brief break in precipitation this weekend. An active weather pattern resumes early next week with a series of systems moving across the region.
hydrology: River levels should continue to gradually fall with the Skokomish expected to recede below flood stage tonight. Additional rises to the Skokomish are possible next week with additional incoming precipitation, but a large degree of uncertainty remains over the extended forecast.

sections.title: Synopsis
paragraphs: Precipitation chances will linger today as a weak system brings light rain to the lowlands and light snow to the Cascades. A weak ridge building over the Pacific Northwest will bring a brief break in precipitation this weekend. An active weather pattern resumes early next week with a series of systems moving across the region.

sections.title: Short term (today through Sunday)
paragraphs: Much quieter conditions prevail across Western Washington this morning compared to this time yesterday with just a few spotty showers and lighter winds. Precipitation associated with a stalled frontal boundary over Oregon will spread northward into the area later today, but it will be considerably lighter than what we saw on Thanksgiving morning. With a cooler air mass in place, we'll see some light snowfall in the passes. But it is expected to fall short of any headlines. Shortwave ridging will slide across the region late tonight into Saturday for a short reprieve from the recent active weather.

Another developing system moves into the offshore waters on Sunday with some rain spreading inland across Western Washington through the course of the day. Models do not have a good handle on the track and strength of the surface low. Parts of Western Washington will likely see windy conditions developing by Sunday night, but the path of the low will define a lot of the details. And we'll discuss that in the long term discussion.

Coastal flooding remains a threat for many areas heading into the weekend. Areas along the north interior coastline are favored to see the highest degree of coastal flooding over the weekend, with lesser impacts expected elsewhere.

sections.title: Long term (Sunday night through Thursday)
paragraphs: As alluded to in the short term discussion, the path of a surface low Sunday night into Monday could have significant implications in terms of the wind forecast. Models solutions range from a weakening surface low tracking into northern Vancouver Island to a concerning 00Z operational ECMWF showing a sub 985 millibar low making landfall over Grays Harbor county early Monday AM and tracking northeastward across the CWA. Stay tuned to the forecast as models get a better handle as to how this is expected to play out.

There is a trend toward a somewhat quieter period of weather as we move toward the middle of the coming week with the storm track diving southward into California. This pattern favors anomalous weak ridging just offshore. While this doesn't imply an entirely dry forecast, it does favor somewhat more benign conditions as systems moving into British Columbia clip the area.
Additional coastal flooding may occur into next week due to high astronomical tides.

sections.title: Aviation
paragraphs: Westerly flow aloft this morning as a weak system will move through western Washington late this morning and afternoon. Rain will start to move through the area 14z-19z, with conditions lowering to MVFR through most area terminals. In heavier showers, could see reduced visibilities around 3 to 5SM at times. MVFR conditions will likely continue through the rest of the afternoon and evening hours for most area terminals. S/SW winds this morning generally around 9 to 14 kts will decrease to around 5 to 10 knots this afternoon, decreasing later this evening to 4 to 8 knots.

KSEA...VFR early this morning with a weak system moving into the area this afternoon. Rain will start to spread near the terminal around 18z-20z, with conditions lowering to MVFR. Reductions in visibilities will be likely during this time, around 3 to 6 SM at times. S/SW winds 5 to 10 knots this morning, decreasing generally throughout the day to 4 to 8 knots, maintaining the same direction.
Mazurkiewicz

sections.title: Marine
paragraphs: Winds will continue throughout the day with Small Craft Advisories continuing for the coastal waters, mainly due to elevated seas. A weak system will approach the area waters today, with minimal impacts to wind and seas. High pressure will then develop over the coastal waters through the weekend, with wind and seas further easing. The exception is the Strait of Juan De Fuca, where a westerly push of winds is likely.

A low pressure looks to move into the area Monday into Tuesday, for increasing winds and seas. Latest guidance is a bit shaky on the exact tracking of the low pressure system, which could impact the strength of the winds. Will continue to monitor as more guidance becomes available.

Coastal seas generally 10 to 15 this morning decreasing to below 10 early this evening. Seas will decrease even further to 4 to 6 over the weekend, before the aforementioned system moves in on Monday, increasing seas upwards to 15 to 18 feet.
Mazurkiewicz

sections.title: Hydrology
paragraphs: River levels should continue to gradually fall with the Skokomish expected to recede below flood stage tonight. Additional rises to the Skokomish are possible next week with additional incoming precipitation, but a large degree of uncertainty remains over the extended forecast.

discussions.name: NWS Portland
synopsis: A low pressure system will bring another round of steady rain on Friday, with periods of moderate to heavy rain for some locations. Dry weather and offshore winds return Saturday. Active weather returns Sunday into Monday with rain and windy conditions. A break from rain and wind expected late Tuesday into Wednesday before rain returns Thursday.

sections.title: Synopsis
paragraphs: A low pressure system will bring another round of steady rain on Friday, with periods of moderate to heavy rain for some locations. Dry weather and offshore winds return Saturday. Active weather returns Sunday into Monday with rain and windy conditions. A break from rain and wind expected late Tuesday into Wednesday before rain returns Thursday.

sections.title: Discussion
paragraphs: Now through Thursday...Showers continue across NW OR and SW WA early Friday morning as moisture associated with Thursday's atmospheric river continues funneling into the region along the zonal upper level flow that has set up in the wake of Thursday's low pressure system. A shortwave along the flow will tap into this existing moisture as it moves east through the eastern Pacific towards the coast this morning, then pushes inland later today. Rain will become more widespread and heavier later this morning then slowly push south late this afternoon and evening. Between 4 AM today through 4 AM Saturday, there's a 65-75% chance for locations west of the Cascade foothills to receive at least 1 inch of rain with similar probabilities for the Cascades and foothills to receive at least 2 inches of rain. Not every location will exceed these amounts; instead, locations that receive higher rain rates could. Expect periods of heavy rain once again with a 15-30% chance of rain rates exceeding 0.2-0.25 inch per hour this afternoon and early evening. Rain rates of this magnitude are high enough to bring continued chances for nuisance urban flooding in areas with poor drainage. This will bring an increased risk of hydroplaning for motorists due to ponding of water on roads. Be sure to slow down and never drive on a flooded road.

Dry weather returns for Saturday as brief upper level ridging moves inland behind today's shortwave, though don't expect much sunshine as clouds will continue moving into the area ahead of the next weather system. Specific details remain uncertain this far out, but what is clear is this system will bring additional widespread rain Sunday morning and continue into Monday as well as breezy winds Sunday night into Monday. The amount of moisture associated with this system is less than the previous two systems. In the 48 hour period of 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM Tuesday, there's a 40-60% chance for the interior lowlands to receive at least 1 inch of rain and a 30-50% chance for the coast and terrain to receive at least 2 inches of rain, lower chances compared to the 24 hour chances with today's weather system. Snow levels will fall from north to south through Monday behind the frontal passage to around 4500-5500 ft. However, precipitation amounts are forecast to also decrease through the day, which will limit snow amounts over the passes. NBM indicates very high chances for at least 0.01 inch of snow at passes and locations above 4500 ft. However, probabilities dwindle quite significantly when looking at 1-2 inches at pass level to 5-25%. At this point, not expecting significant impacts due to snow.

What could be more impactful is the potential breezy winds Sunday night into Monday morning as many ensemble members indicate the surface low strengthening as it approaches the north OR/south WA coast and moves north towards BC just along the coast line. NBM indicates a 30-50% chance of peak wind gusts exceeding 58 mph (High Wind Warning criteria) along the direct coast, beaches and headlands and a 15-30% chance for inland coastal communities such as Astoria and Tillamook. There's also a 15-35% chance for peak wind gusts exceeding 45 mph (Wind Advisory criteria) for the interior excluding the high Cascades. Gusts of this strength could cause downed trees and power outages, especially as soils begin to saturate from continued weather systems.

There's a 10-35% chance of light showers continuing into Tuesday, highest over the coast and terrain, as a weak trough originating from Alaska with limited moisture moves through the PacNW. Cold air moves in behind this trough, dropping daytime temperatures into the mid 40s for the interior lowlands for Wednesday. Additionally, ensembles are confident in dry weather returning again on Wednesday, at least for inland locations, due to ridging behind Tuesday's trough. Dry weather is not expected to last long as ensembles indicate another weather system quickly bringing more precipitation to the area sometime late Wednesday into Thursday. -03

sections.title: Aviation
paragraphs: Through 12z Saturday...Current rain will become more widespread and increase in intensity through Friday, spreading from north to south. There is high confidence that the current mix of VFR and MVFR conditions will trend more IFR/MVFR (60-80%) by 14z Fri and lasting throughout the day. Moderate to locally heavy rain at times may also lead to VIS reductions to 4-5 SM. As rain ends from north to south, conditions expected to improve to VFR for inland terminals, generally after 02-06z Sat. Winds under 10 kts, generally variable or southerly, then turning northerly after 18-21z Fri except after 00z Sat in the southern Willamette Valley.

KPDX AND APPROACHES...Predominately MVFR conditions with low-end MVFR (1-2 kft) conditions expected through 00-03z Fri as rain continues at the terminal. Heavier showers could produce brief IFR conditions. As rain ends after 00-03z Fri, conditions expected to improve to VFR. Winds generally under 5 kts becoming north to northeast after 18-20z Fri. -03

sections.title: Marine
paragraphs: Buoy observations early Friday morning indicate wave heights have fallen to 11-13 ft at 12-14 seconds with winds below 15 kts. Conditions will remain steady today as another weather system moves through the waters. A Small Craft Advisory remains in effect through 1 AM Saturday until seas fall below 10 ft.

A brief break in active weather will see calmer marine conditions on Saturday into early Sunday with seas falling to 5-7 ft. However, another weather system will impact the waters Sunday afternoon into early next week. There is 50-75% chance of gales Sunday night into Monday. A strong southwesterly swell also builds over the coastal waters associated with this weather system during the same time. Confidence is high (60-70% chance) wave heights exceed 15 ft again late Sunday into Monday, with a 25-40% chance of exceeding 20 ft. -03

sections.title: Beach hazards
paragraphs: The combination of King Tides and elevated seas leading to tidal overflow continue to support a Coastal Flood Advisory through Friday for the south Washington coast. Impacts during this period are most likely in the hours around high tide. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and property. There is also a continued moderate to high sneaker wave threat through Friday as well. Beachgoers should exercise caution, stay far back from incoming waves, and remain observant of the ocean. Avoid logs, large rocks, and jetties.
